Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)  
- Clinical presentation consistent with uncomplicated urinary tract infection (cystitis): dysuria for 6 days, unpleasant urine smell, hematuria (spotting), intermittent lower central abdominal pain rated 7/10, no fever or systemic symptoms  
- Differential diagnoses supported and ranked by DDx:  
  • Urinary tract infection (cystitis) – High likelihood due to classic symptom pattern and absence of systemic signs  
  • Urolithiasis (bladder or urethral stones) – Moderate likelihood given hematuria and pain, but no flank pain or history of stones  
  • Urethritis (possibly STI-related) – Moderate likelihood but less likely given absence of discharge, sexual risk factors, or systemic symptoms  
  • Bladder neoplasm – Low likelihood due to age, acute onset, and lack of constitutional symptoms  
- No evidence or history suggestive of trauma, medication-induced cystitis, congenital abnormalities, or endocrine causes  
- Allergy: Clindamycin  

Management Plan  
- Initiate 3-day course of antibiotics (specific antibiotic not documented) prescribed and sent electronically to patient’s chosen pharmacy (Knightsbridge Practice)  
- Advise increased fluid intake: 2.5–3 liters per day  
- Advise symptomatic measures: cranberry juice and urinary alkalinizing sachets available over the counter; details to be added in notes  
- Patient instructed to monitor temperature using home thermometer (to be acquired) and observe for development of fever, worsening pain, lower back pain, difficulty urinating, or recurrence of symptoms  
- Advise to seek follow-up if symptoms worsen, do not resolve after antibiotics, or recur to consider further investigation  
- No immediate investigations or referrals made during this consultation
